question: Asha bought a mixer for ₹2,160 and sold it for ₹1,998. Find the loss percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 2160 : 1998

Dividing both sides by 54, we get CP : SP = 40 : 37

Loss in ratio parts = 40 − 37 = 3 parts

Loss % = (Loss parts ÷ CP parts) × 100

Loss % = (3 ÷ 40) × 100 = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the mixer = ₹2160

Selling Price (SP) of the mixer = ₹1998

 
 Cost Price (CP) = ₹2160

 
 Selling Price (SP) = ₹1998

 
 Loss

 
• 
 
• 

 Loss % = (162 ÷ 2160) × 100 = 7.5%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Loss = 2160 − 1998

⇒ Loss = ₹162

⇒ Loss % = (162 ÷ 2160) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 1620 ÷ 216

⇒ Loss % = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base of Calculation

Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the question.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). The fundamental relationship is given by: SP = MP − Discount.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer claims to sell at CP but uses a false weight, his actual CP is based on the false weight given, while SP is based on the claimed weight.
